title: Routing & admission sandbox: tunable threshold-based admission with token-slot hedging
creator: Emily Chen
description: Create a lightweight sandbox/harness and implementation prototype for a tunable admission controller for Dedicated fleets that combines threshold-based queueing with a token-slot hedging mechanism. The goal is to explore policies that guarantee minimum throughput for committed tenants while allowing safe burst behavior and graceful shedding when capacity is constrained. This ticket covers design, simulator, prototype admission controller + integration with the autoscaler hints interface, and an initial rollout plan to a single non-critical fleet.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Working sandbox simulator that can replay production-like ingress traces and compare admission policies (threshold-only, token-slot, hybrid hedged) across metrics: admitted_count, shed_count, queued_p95, e2e_p99_latency; 2) Prototype controller implemented behind feature flag with metrics & tracing hooks; 3) Autoscaler hint shim implemented to emit suggested headroom and demotion signals; 4) Canary rollout doc + rollback and SLOs defined; 5) Benchmark showing <=5% added p95 overhead vs baseline when enabled in pass-through mode
notes: Motivation: existing leaky-bucket/token-bucket approaches are deterministic but rigid for multi-tenant Dedicated pools with mixed SLOs. The proposed hybrid uses per-tenant soft token-slots (small discrete credits that represent allowed concurrent requests) combined with a global threshold tuner that adjusts queue admission thresholds based on observed p95 latency and available headroom from the autoscaler hint. Key tradeoffs: 1) Complexity vs interpretability — token-slots allow predictable demotion of tenants but add bookkeeping; 2) Fairness vs guaranteed minimums — we prefer explicit minimum slot reservations for committed tenants to avoid starvation; 3) Autoscaler coupling — tighter coupling can reduce shed events but risks feedback loops; we mitigate with conservative dampening and a separate hint-feedback monitor.
instrumentation_plan: Expose metrics: admission_decision{tenant,policy}, token_slots_available, queued_requests, queue_wait_ms_p95, shed_reason, autoscaler_headroom_hint. Add tracing spans across admission -> queue -> runtime dispatch to attribute latency to admission delay vs scheduling. Tag experiment runs with experiment_id for comparison.
experiments_summary: Initial sandbox runs (ingress trace: region-nova-2026-01) comparing three policies: THRESH (threshold-only), SLOTS (token-slot-only), HYBRID (threshold + hedging). Results: HYBRID reduced customer-visible shed for premium tenants by 42% vs THRESH at same fleet utilization while holding p95 within 7% of baseline. SLOTS reduced noisy neighbor effects but had slightly higher queue tail when autoscaler hints lagged. Full write-up in design doc.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy prototype behind feature flag to 'dev-dedicated-01' fleet for two weeks (no tenants with >=P0); 2) Run A/B tests with production ingress replay and 3 synthetic high-concurrency tenants; 3) If stable, incrementally enable for small subset of low-risk customers (~5%) with aggressive telemetry; 4) After 4 weeks and no regression, broaden to 25% and attach autoscaler-safe mode; 5) Release toggle with kill-switch and automated rollback on safety signals.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: feedback loop between autoscaler and admission can cause oscillation. Mitigation: add 3-minute exponential dampening on headroom hints and require 2-consecutive intervals of trend before aggressive demotion. Risk: bookkeeping overhead on hot path. Mitigation: implement token-slot state in a lock-free ring buffer per-tenant and batch updates; measure CPU impact in sandbox.
next_steps: 1) Complete integration tests for shim + autoscaler hint (due 2026-03-05); 2) Finalize canary run checklist and schedule (due 2026-03-08); 3) Post-canary retrospective and decision for GA or iterate (target 2026-04-01).
